summary: Zero-shot text-to-speech that speaks in a voice from one reference clip, with emotion control, in Chinese, English and more.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: IndexTTS is a text-to-speech system from bilibili that copies a speaker's voice from a single reference audio clip. The latest release, IndexTTS-2.5, supports Chinese, English, Japanese, Spanish and Arabic, and lets you control emotion with a separate emotional reference clip, an emotion vector, or a text description. It comes with a web demo and a Python API.
sixtySeconds.problem: Most TTS voices sound flat and fixed. IndexTTS lets you pick a voice from a short sample and steer its emotion.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for multilingual zero-shot TTS with fine-grained emotion control and a ready web demo.
requirements: NVIDIA GPU recommended; CUDA Toolkit 12.8 or newer if you see CUDA errors

overview: Clone the repo and run uv sync --all-extras, which creates a virtual environment with the right Python and dependencies.
Download the model weights from Hugging Face or ModelScope into the checkpoints folder.
Start the web demo with uv run webui.py and open http://127.0.0.1:7860. Use is governed by the bilibili Model Use License Agreement; read the DISCLAIMER too.

Don't activate another environment before uv commands; uv activates the right one.
Start the WebUI once, or run the README's ensure_examples_available command.
